item.title: June 2026 - Deepseek API For Performance & Cost
item.description: (following post has been updated 5th of july, 2026) Intro A shift in LLM/AI usage: GitHub Copilot changed its user pricing. Microsoft changed the pricing. Nvidia & AMD are coming up with new laptops with 128 or more GB of VRAM to run agents and LLMs locally! But the prices of the chips are not going down; at the time of writing, the Nvidia RTX 5070 16GB is 65k INR.

item.title: Comparing Free Chinese Models For Daily Use - May 2026
item.description: Intro I wanted to test the performance and accuracy of the ai models at the time of writing this (May 2026, so I can leverage them in my day-to-day tasks). Currently, I am testing 3 models: 1. Deepseek (v4 just got released) 2. GLM 3. Qwen. Identifying a common task At the time of writing this, there are Tamil Nadu elections. I’ve made up my mind to ask the AI to visualize the TN elections and would rate them based on their accuracy and how beautifully they present the data.

item.title: Offline AI models on Phones & PC - April 2026
item.description: Intro Today I want to talk about, Google Gemma 4; this sets a new standard for open source AI models. I am astonished by the quality of this, though it has a small model size compared to the other big ones out there.. like Kimi K2.5 from Moonshot AI, that thing is a 1 trillion parameter model.. 1 trillion! and Gemma 4’s biggest is only 31 billion.. but here is the thing, Kimi K2.

item.title: 'AI Skills'
item.description: Intro Anthropic came and published their skills documentation on what they are roughly 2 months ago, but I suspect they and other AI companies were using them internally even before they published. The idea of people seeing them as a new thing and being astonished is abysmal..because we were already using it..but without the naming convention and the optimised context limiting. The concept is simple: you create a folder named skill you want, then inside it, the main file is called skill.

item.title: Local Agent Workflows
item.description: Intro I’ve been mentioning these things in my previous posts. I don’t use AI to write these, but I use them as a way to fix spelling and grammar mistakes. There is also another way that I use these tools for, and that is for local workflows. Local workflows help writing automation scripts in natural language; you don’t have to write code and handle edge cases to cover it. Give an example and it will take it over.

item.title: "Slop Generators - Make no mistake, they cannot think", as of Nov 25th, 2025
item.description: Quote I liked from Asahi Linux I’ve read the quote, in an open source AI contribution page, exact word for word, quote https://asahilinux.org/docs/project/policies/slop/#its-just-matmul “It is very easy to get caught up in the hype that bad actors have built around Slop Generators. The anthropomorphic presentation of Slop Generators as “agents” or “assistants” is a very deliberate attempt to manufacture consent for their integration into workforces at the expense of human interaction.

item.title: Using the best thinking models and not burn money (Jul 31st, 2025)
item.description: Intro I’ve been having a dilemma, I don’t want to pay open ai the monthly 20$ subscription, but I want to use the latest and greatest model on some of the problems I have to reduce time. How can I achieve this? I’ve already mentioned in a previous writing last year.. that I use open api keys. I started using mobile and desktop clients with just the api keys. Couple months ago OpenAI also reduced the pricing of o3 model by 80%, I’ve been using the ai very actively, trying to burn my credits as soon as possible.

item.title: My Stab at Using Ai for Productivity
item.description: My ai usecases Purchasing AI - Using It as API vs Monthly Subscription for ChatGPT/Claude Do you need to buy monthly subscriptions? Take Copilot and other examples. To test this out, I bought $5 worth of usage from OpenAI, used an extension for VSCode for ai operations, and used ai tools that require api token..like AI Commits. Did it work? Yes. Have I used all of those $5? No, it’s still there.
